run.procedureSummary: Feed: add the cycle's feed row to every chamber, ignoring holding limits. Carry forward: go through chambers 1 to 6 in order. Any amount over a chamber's holding limit is cut back to the limit and added to the next chamber before that chamber's turn, so a chamber can pass on excess it received from the one before. Chamber 6's excess goes to the loss tally. State check: a LARVAL chamber at or above its upper mark turns PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber at or below its lower mark turns LARVAL. Every change is logged. Metabolism: amounts are worked out from the contents before the step and applied to all chambers at once. LARVAL loses floor(q/4) to the tally. PUPAL gives floor(q/2) to the previous chamber; for chamber 1 it goes to the tally. Contents left over the limit stay put until the next carry forward. Moult: if the line total after metabolism is strictly over 38, each chamber becomes floor(q/2) and the amount removed (q - floor(q/2)) goes to the tally.

openPoints.point: Moult rounding: does 'halves, rounded down' set the remaining mass or the removed mass?
openPoints.assumption: The remaining mass is floor(q/2) and the removed amount q - floor(q/2) goes to the tally. For an odd q this removes the larger half.

openPoints.point: When the moult test happens and which total it uses
openPoints.assumption: It uses the line total after metabolism, with a strict test (total > 38). In cycle 5 the total was exactly 38, so the moult did not fire.
Yes. Chambers are processed in order, so excess received from the previous chamber counts toward the next chamber's own overflow.
Amounts are taken from a snapshot of the contents before the step, so reabsorbed mass a chamber receives does not change its own loss. All moves are applied together.

openPoints.point: Which state the metabolism step uses
openPoints.assumption: It uses the state after this cycle's state check.
Both are inclusive (at or above the upper mark; at or below the lower mark). Each chamber is checked once per cycle, so it changes state at most once per cycle.
